affectedCopies: No new copies. GppPermit and GppPermitObservation are still read only by the GPP verdict code (apps/web/lib/gpp); no projection, graph mirror or AI context reads them.
ToolExecution.gppPermitVerdict duplicates the observation's verdict onto the existing audit row by design (PR-C); it now can hold the five added verdicts.

The signed handle (gpp1.<permitId>.<keyId>.<mac>) is returned to the in-process caller on GovernedExecuteResult.governance.permit and is not persisted anywhere else. The handler and the audit row keep only the opaque permit id.

privacyAssessment.sensitivity: internal: security-audit evidence. paramHash is a one-way SHA-256 of the call's canonical arguments; the arguments themselves are never stored. mac is an HMAC over the permit's own claims; the signing key is never stored in the database.
privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: not-applicable: this change adds no personal data. The rows keep PR-C's 365-day telemetry-bounded security-audit retention.
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: Audit-only, still shadow: no verdict changes a call's outcome. Read by operators and the later per-binding promotion review (PR-E).

migration.name: 20261001200000_gpp_permit_mac_verdicts
migration.backfill: None. The migration only adds the GppPermitVerdict members mac_invalid, param_mismatch, lineage_unsealed, lineage_missing and unsigned (ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS) and touches no row, so it applies identically to an empty table and one full of PR-C verdicts. Permits minted before this change keep null paramHash, keyRef and mac; their verdicts record the parameter check as not_bound.
migration.rollback: Forward-only. Postgres cannot drop an enum member; reverting the code leaves the members unused, and PR-C's verdicts continue.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Existing model (PR-C); unchanged @dpf lifecycle=telemetry-bounded retention=365d. PR-D populates three columns PR-C created as nullable.

fields.reason: SHA-256 (hex) over canonicalJson({ tool, params }) of the admitted call, bound at mint; a replay with other arguments is recorded as param_mismatch. One-way; the arguments are not stored.
fields.provenance: Written only by apps/web/lib/gpp/permit-mint.ts (via lib/gpp/permit-store.ts) using lib/gpp/param-hash.ts; BI-69415B68 PR-D.

fields.reason: Id of the DPF_GPP_PERMIT_SECRET key that signed the claims; null when the install has no key (verdict unsigned). Never the key itself.
fields.provenance: Written only by apps/web/lib/gpp/permit-mint.ts (via lib/gpp/permit-store.ts) from lib/gpp/permit-handle.ts signPermit.

fields.reason: base64url HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical claims, so an edited or invented row is detected (mac_invalid); null when unsigned.
fields.provenance: Written only by apps/web/lib/gpp/permit-mint.ts (via lib/gpp/permit-store.ts) from lib/gpp/permit-handle.ts signPermit.

fields.reason: The GppPermitVerdict enum gains mac_invalid, param_mismatch, lineage_unsealed, lineage_missing and unsigned. Additive only.
fields.provenance: Written only by apps/web/lib/gpp/permit-verdict.ts and lib/gpp/unmediated-observation.ts (via lib/gpp/permit-store.ts).

fields.reason: Now also carries checks: the outcome of the MAC, parameter-hash, lineage and state checks, plus the handle format. Never parameters, results, the handle's MAC or the key.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Existing model; the column follows the row's existing 365-day lifecycle and adds no retention obligation.
